narrative: The model estimated a 64% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that estimate crossed the denial threshold, your law school application was rejected. The strongest factor was your third-year class-standing decile of 4, which is below the average of about 5.8 among accepted students; this pushed the prediction most strongly toward likely bar-exam failure. Your LSAT score of 38.5 was the second most important factor and pushed toward passing, since it is slightly above the accepted-student average of about 37.2. Your first-year decile of 6 was the third most important factor and added a smaller push toward failure, even though it matched the accepted average. Your gender and race were not used in this decision. To improve your position, ask the admissions office for specific feedback, provide context or evidence of academic improvement, and consider retaking the LSAT if a higher score is realistic. You should also build a concrete bar-exam preparation plan and discuss it with an advisor, then reapply with a stronger application that directly addresses the third-year academic concern.
